label: D2 after choosing a1 and reaching S1 (common a1->S1 transition)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (DELAY_2), and only when the last-action input is a1 and the state shown is S1, i.e. the common a1->S1 transition. Recall is 1.0 on dev: it never fires at D1 or GO, never on a2 trials, and never on rare transitions (a1->S2) or a2->S1. Uses only observed inputs. The predicate is true on about 14% of steps where the feature stays silent; these are mostly the first a1->S1 trial right after switching from a2, and long runs of rewarded a1->S1 trials, where activation fades to near zero. Magnitude: highest (top quartile) when the previous trial was unrewarded or rare (71% of the top quartile vs about 25% of the lower quartiles), and it falls off steadily over consecutive rewarded common S1 trials. Adding prev_action != 2 increases precision a little but lowers F1, so the simple version was recorded.

issues: The explanation gets the false positives wrong. It is not true that they are 'mostly the first a1->S1 trial right after a switch from a2'. When the previous trial was a2 and common-unrewarded, the predicate's precision is 0.868 (test, n=5577), so switches after a2 common-unrewarded fire normally. The predicate fails after a2 rare-rewarded (precision 0.254, n=4090).

It is also not true that long runs of rewarded a1->S1 trials make up most of the false positives. When the last two trials were both a1 common-rewarded, precision is 0.907 (n=25502), which is higher than the base rate of 0.856.

There is one systematic class of silent steps the explanation leaves out: the previous trial was rare AND rewarded. The predicate restricted to prev_common==0 & prev_reward==1 has precision 0.149 over 9053 test steps, about 7700 false positives, or roughly 40% of all false positives. Both directions are silent: after a1->S2 rare-rewarded, precision is 0.063 (n=4963), and after a2->S1 rare-rewarded, 0.254. After a rare-unrewarded previous trial the feature fires almost always (a1 rare-unrewarded: 0.996).

The magnitude claim says activation is 'highest when the previous trial was unrewarded or rare'. That is only half right: after a rare-rewarded previous trial the feature is usually completely silent. The silencing partly carries over two trials back (0.38 precision when trial -2 was rare-rewarded and trial -1 was rewarded).

Claims that check out: the feature fires only at D2 (zero at D1 and GO), only when in_action==1 and in_state==1, test recall is 0.99995 with 6 scattered misses, and the predicate uses only observed variables.

Adding the observed exclusion ~((prev_common==0)&(prev_reward==1)) raises test F1 from 0.922 to 0.946 (precision 0.907, recall 0.988); dev F1 is 0.946. Most of the remaining false positives are window-first trials where prev_common is unknown.
skeptic.revised_label: D2 after choosing a1 and reaching S1 (common a1->S1), unless the previous trial was a rare transition that was rewarded
